Article Title: China hits $1 trillion trade surplus milestone for second year in a row
Article Text:
Representative image

AI demand supports exports, but trade tensions persist

Weak domestic demand adds to export dependence

Oil imports fall despite supply concerns

China's trade surplus crossed $1 trillion in the first 10 months of the year, as strong global demand for high-tech products, fuelled by the race to build artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, helped offset weak domestic consumption.The surplus reached $1.04 trillion between January and October, according to customs data released on Tuesday.China has now recorded a trade surplus of more than $1 trillion for a second consecutive year, reaching the milestone a month earlier than in 2025.Exports rose 35.2% in October from a year earlier in US dollar terms, slightly below September's 36.3% increase but higher than the 33.5% growth forecast by economists in a Reuters poll.Imports grew 41.6%, accelerating from 31% in September and beating the poll's median forecast of 32%.Despite the stronger import growth, China's trade surplus narrowed to $105.3 billion in October from $133.5 billion in September.The export performance reflects China's growing reliance on overseas demand as subdued domestic consumption and a prolonged property market downturn weigh on its economy.The global AI investment boom has supported sales of Chinese technology products, including semiconductors and electronics, but the expanding surplus is also raising concerns among trading partners.Much of China's export growth this year has been driven by the global push to expand AI infrastructure. Analysts expect demand for Chinese technology products to remain strong into 2027, although the outlook will depend on how long the investment boom lasts.“The outlook for exports depends on how long the AI boom will last,” Macquarie analysts wrote, adding that exports could accelerate further in the fourth quarter before beginning to slow from the first quarter of 2027.Dave Chia, an economist at Moody's Analytics, also expects Chinese exports to remain strong through the rest of the year, led by electronics and automobiles.However, the expanding surplus could intensify trade tensions, particularly with the European Union.European leaders have called for further trade restrictions on China after reaching an agreement with Beijing to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle exports to the bloc over the next few years.Since the measures have yet to take effect, manufacturers are expected to bring forward shipments, supporting exports in the near term.“The risk of additional tariffs and other trade barriers will remain elevated in 2027, particularly as Chinese manufacturers continue expanding their presence in overseas markets,” said Joe Peissel, lead macroeconomist at Trivium China.The US-China trade relationship also remains uncertain. Beijing on Monday officially announced a two-month extension of its trade truce with Washington, which was due to expire on November 10.However, China said last week that any expansion of its purchases of US agricultural goods would depend on the implementation of the agreed reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement.China's trade surplus with the US narrowed slightly to $32.71 billion in October from $34.01 billion in September, but the gap remains a point of friction between the two economies.Trade is expected to feature prominently in the planned meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen later this month.The two leaders are expected to meet for the third time this year.The strong export performance comes against the backdrop of subdued consumer spending in China. A prolonged downturn in the property market has weakened household wealth and confidence, leaving domestic demand under pressure.The weakness has also pushed Chinese manufacturers to look overseas for customers. Automobile exports maintained a solid pace of growth in October, while domestic vehicle sales recorded their 12th consecutive monthly decline, according to separate industry data.AP cited analysts who said overcapacity in several industries, excess domestic savings and weak domestic demand were pushing Chinese companies to sell more goods abroad. Alicia García-Herrero, chief economist for Asia Pacific at Natixis, said the situation was not sustainable.Businesses are also facing intense competition at home. Cinders Zhou, who sells eyewear for a manufacturer in the eastern Chinese city of Linhai, told AP that competition had increasingly centred on price as products across the industry became more similar.“It comes down to product quality, or rather the increasingly the lack of it across the industry, since there's significant homogenization,” Zhou said. “That has forced everyone to compete on price.”Greater dependence on overseas markets also leaves China's economy more exposed to a slowdown in global demand or further trade restrictions. Analysts have warned that any correction in the AI industry could hurt exports of chips and electronics.“If the AI boom slows or turns into a correction, lower chip and electronics prices and smaller shipping volumes would hit China's exports hard,” Chia said, according to AP.China's oil imports fell 13.3% in October compared with a year earlier, although shipments reached their highest level since March as buyers sought supplies following disruptions to Middle East flows caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran.The trade figures come ahead of the APEC summit, where trade policy and tariffs are expected to be among the key issues in discussions between Trump and Xi. The two sides had previously proposed a $60 billion package of reciprocal tariff cuts following their September summit in Washington, including around $17 billion worth of US agricultural goods.While Chinese officials have maintained that Beijing is not seeking to expand its trade surplus and wants more balanced global trade, the latest figures underline the importance of overseas demand to the country's export-led growth.
Article Summary: Exports rose 35.2% in October from a year earlier in US dollar terms, slightly below September's 36.3% increase. Imports grew 41.6%, accelerating from 31% in September and beating the poll's median forecast of 32%. Despite the stronger import growth, China's trade surplus narrowed to $105.3 billion in October.

Article Title: As gold falls from Rs 1.8 lakh peak to Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams, Indians buy 30% more, spending Rs 72,000 crore on 52 tonnes; silver demand rises 10%
Article Text:
In the current fiscal year through September, gold sales by volume declined by nearly 50%.

Gold price correction from Rs 1.8 lakh peak

Gold generates big returns

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Gold prices falling from their record highs has led to Indian consumers increasing their purchases of precious metals during the Dhanteras-Diwali period. Gold demand rose 30% in volume terms and silver buying grew 10% compared with the corresponding period last year, according to the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA). Jewellers said the trend pointed to a recovery in demand ahead of the important wedding season.The industry body estimated that consumers purchased 52 tonnes of gold worth Rs 72,000 crore and 300 tonnes of silver valued at Rs 5,400 crore during this year’s Dhanteras and Diwali celebrations.The increase followed a correction in gold prices from a peak of around Rs 1.8 lakh to Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams, drawing buyers back into the market. Purchases made in advance of the wedding season, which starts in mid-November and runs until March, also helped boost demand.“Jewellers have made good business in this year’s Dhanteras and Diwali,” IBJA national secretary Surendra Mehta told ET.Mehta said the market was witnessing pent-up demand, as several consumers had put off buying gold after Prime Minister Narendra Modi appealed to people not to purchase the metal.“Consumers had stayed away from the precious metal. But since the price has fallen and there is a chance of prices moving northwards again as Brent crude prices have fallen, people have come out to buy gold. In fact, buying is still continuing .”The festival calendar also worked in favour of jewellery purchases. Dhanteras was observed on November 6, followed by Diwali on November 8. Both occasions fell in the early part of the month, when salaried employees typically receive their monthly pay and festive bonuses.“This has resulted in healthy cash flow in the market, encouraging consumers to shop enthusiastically. Gold prices have also been relatively lower over the past four to six months, further improving purchasing sentiment,” said Rajesh Rokde, chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council.In the current fiscal year through September, gold sales by volume declined by nearly 50%. The fall was attributed to higher prices, an increase in import duty and Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s appeal to consumers to refrain from buying gold.Despite the volatility, gold has generated significant returns over the past few years. Prices, which were around Rs 60,000 per 10 grams in 2023, climbed to Rs 80,000 in 2024 and reached Rs 1.15 lakh-Rs 1.20 lakh in 2025. During this year’s Dhanteras-Diwali period, prices stood at approximately Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams. Silver has also recorded a substantial appreciation in value.An analysis of eight years of business performance by Bengaluru-based C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers found that gold sales volumes during this festive season were the third-highest in a decade, even though prices were around 10% above their level a year earlier.“The overall sentiment has remained unshaken, with consumers continuing to repose confidence in gold jewellery despite the unprecedented rise in prices over a 12-month period,” said C Vinod Hayagriv, director of C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers.Natural diamonds also held up well, registering their second-highest sales volume in eight years. The retailer recorded a 250% increase in natural diamond sales on Dhanteras, while sales during the Diwali season rose 47%.The performance comes at a time when the natural diamond industry is facing disruption from global sanctions affecting Russian diamond supplies and increasing competition from lab-grown alternatives. However, lab-grown diamonds are emerging as an additional product category rather than displacing natural diamonds.
Article Summary: Indian consumers increased their purchases of precious metals during the Dhanteras-Diwali period. Gold demand rose 30% in volume terms and silver buying grew 10% compared with the corresponding period last year. Jewellers said the trend pointed to a recovery in demand ahead of the important wedding season.

Article Title: Nvidia loses $500 billion since last week amid 'spy' scandal; Jensen Huang slips to 13th on Forbes rich list
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after reports came out on multiple affairs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia shares plunged as much as 14 per cent during Thursday's Wall Street trading session after the shock resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang, extending a weeks-long selloff in the chipmaker amid concerns over the company's leadership and the future of the artificial intelligence boom. The stock recovered some of its losses during the session, eventually closing 4.3 per cent lower at $166.19.The latest decline has dealt another blow to Nvidia's market valuation, with the company shedding nearly $500 billion in market value since the close of trading last week. Its shares are now around 30 per cent below the record high touched on October 6, wiping out more than $1 trillion in market capitalisation over the past month. Nvidia's market value slipped below $4 trillion, a level it had not breached since July 2025, reported Reuters. Huang has lost his spot in world's top 10 richest people.The selloff marks a sharp reversal for a company that became the world's most valuable publicly listed business on the back of the global AI boom. Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs), which power artificial intelligence systems and data centres, made it a central player in the technology industry and one of Wall Street's biggest market drivers.Its shares had surged more than 1,700% over four years before the recent correction, while its market capitalisation had briefly crossed $5 trillion.Huang's departure has also taken a toll on his personal fortune. The Nvidia co-founder, who had been among the world's 10 richest people, has seen his wealth fall sharply alongside the company's stock. According to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires rankings, he slipped two places from eighth to tenth earlier this week. His estimated fortune subsequently fell further, pushing him out of the top 10 to 13th position.Also read: Trump unsure woman linked to Jensen Huang was a spy; report alleges 3rd affair of ex-Nvidia CEO The fallout extended beyond Nvidia to companies closely linked to its AI ecosystem. Nvidia-backed cloud computing firm CoreWeave fell 8.1 per cent, while Nebius plunged 18 per cent after cutting its 2026 revenue forecast amid delays in adding third-party capacity. Super Micro Computer also dropped 12%. However, rival chipmakers Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom gained more than 4 per cent each, as investors assessed whether Nvidia's leadership turmoil could create opportunities for competitors.Nvidia is also due to report its quarterly results next week, with investors watching its revenue growth and outlook.The turbulence in Nvidia also played out against a volatile session on Wall Street, although the broader market managed to recover most of its early losses. The S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,592.40, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 189.40 points, or 0.4%, to 52,297.09. The Nasdaq Composite also shed 0.4% to close at 25,366.09, after falling as much as 1.6% earlier in the session. Rising oil prices following US President Donald Trump's remarks on Iran added to market pressure, with Brent crude climbing 3.3% to $95.82 a barrel.
Article Summary: N Nvidia shares plunged as much as 14 per cent during Thursday's Wall Street trading session after the shock resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang. The stock recovered some of its losses during the session, eventually closing 4.3 per cent lower at $166.19. The latest decline has dealt another blow to Nvidia's market valuation, with the company shedding nearly $500 billion in market value since the close of trading last week. Huang has lost his spot in world's top 10 richest people.

Article Title: Russia-US diesel deal delivers results? Lavrov claims prices have already fallen
Article Text:
Russia hails diesel deal with US (representative image)

US-bound shipments face uncertainty

Lavrov raises Ukraine strikes on Russian energy infrastructure

Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov has said an agreement allowing Russia to resume diesel exports to the United States and global markets is already being implemented and has helped bring prices down.In an article published in Moscow daily Kommersant on Tuesday, Lavrov said the arrangement was an important contribution to energy security. He also argued that Russia did not use its economy to score political points against countries it considered adversaries or competitors.Also Read| Iran war, cost of living drag Trump’s approval rating near career low: Survey “Since 2022, we have supplied Europe with energy resources worth $320 billion,” Lavrov wrote.“An important contribution to energy security was the agreement between the Russian and US leaders to suspend restrictions on the export of Russian diesel. We have already started implementing it, which immediately brought prices down.”US President Donald Trump announced the deal on October 9. Under the arrangement, Russia agreed to make 300,000 metric tonnes, or 2.25 million barrels, of diesel available immediately to the US and global markets, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and a further 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”.The Trump administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel to facilitate the exports.The move came as the US president sought to bring down fuel prices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which his Republican Party lost.Lavrov did not provide figures to support his claim that the agreement had lowered diesel prices.US diesel futures have fallen about 11% since the deal was announced, according to Reuters.However, diesel prices at US pumps were at a record high last week when Americans voted, according to price tracker GasBuddy.The arrangement has also faced uncertainty over whether Russian fuel would reach the US.Two sanctioned tankers that had initially declared destinations on the US East Coast changed course, while a third vessel travelling across the North Atlantic changed its destination from New York to “for orders”, according to news agency AP.The report said the proposed imports had yet to result in a confirmed US delivery. Analysts also questioned whether the shipments would reach American ports, citing regulatory and sanctions-related concerns.New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill had advised port and terminal operators in the state to reject Russian fuel shipments, warning of possible legal consequences. A bipartisan group of US senators also urged Trump to abandon the arrangement, arguing that it could provide financial support to Moscow.The US Treasury Department, however, maintained that its temporary authorisation for Russian diesel transactions was consistent with previous actions and “in compliance with all applicable laws”.The exemption was issued for the sale, delivery, unloading and import of Russian diesel until April 7.Separately, Russian deputy foreign minister Alexander Pankin said on Monday that the diesel arrangement could provide an opportunity for the gradual restoration of business and other ties between Moscow and Washington.He told the TASS state news agency that the deal could “serve as a foundation for the gradual restoration of business and other ties between our countries”.In his Kommersant article, Lavrov said Russia was working to stabilise global energy markets and ensure energy security, as well as the balanced and sustainable development of countries and regions.He also accused Ukraine of ignoring Trump's calls to stop attacks on Russian energy infrastructure.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said last week that Kyiv's forces were continuing their strikes.Russian media have reported that fuel shortages have returned in at least half a dozen Russian regions following Ukrainian attacks on at least eight major oil refineries over the past two weeks.
Article Summary: Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov hails diesel deal with US. Deal allows Russia to resume diesel exports to the United States and global markets. US President Donald Trump announced the deal on October 9. The arrangement has faced uncertainty over whether Russian fuel would reach the US.

Article Title: Mother Dairy, Amul milk gets costlier: Dairy giant hikes rate by upto Rs 6 per litre from Thursday; check prices
Article Text:
Mother Dairy raises prices

Why are milk prices increasing?

How much will milk cost now?

Full cream milk (packaged): Rs 76 per litre, up from Rs 72.

NEW DELHI: Milk is set to get costlier in Delhi NCR from November 12, with dairy companies Mother Dairy and Amul increasing prices by Rs 2 to Rs 6 per litre. The price hike comes amid lower milk supplies and higher costs of buying milk from farmers.The increase will vary across milk varieties. Toned milk will cost Rs 2 more per litre, full cream milk Rs 4 more and full cream buffalo milk Rs 6 more, according to industry sources.In Delhi-NCR, full cream packaged milk will now cost Rs 76 per litre, compared with Rs 72 earlier. Packaged toned milk will cost Rs 62, up from Rs 60, while toned milk sold through bulk vending machines will cost Rs 60 against Rs 58 earlier.Double-toned milk will become costlier from Rs 54 to Rs 56 per litre. Cow milk prices will rise from Rs 62 to Rs 65, while full cream buffalo milk, which contains 6.5% fat, will cost Rs 86 against Rs 80 earlier.Mother Dairy, the largest milk supplier in Delhi-NCR, had last increased prices on May 14, 2026.Milk procurement has become more expensive for dairy companies. Milk fat prices have risen by around 20-25% over the past few months, while higher cattle feed prices have added to farmers' costs.Milk supplies have also tightened despite the flush season, when production and availability usually improve. The shortage has affected the availability of milk fat, making it more expensive for dairy companies.When fresh milk supplies fall short, companies usually use milk powder and milk fat to prepare liquid milk. However, higher milk fat prices have also increased the cost of this process.Dairy companies have raised the prices they pay farmers to encourage them to produce and supply more milk. Amul has increased the procurement rate linked to milk fat to Rs 1,000 per kilogram. This allows farmers to receive more than Rs 60 per litre for milk, according to industry sources.Mother Dairy has decided to pass on part of these higher costs to consumers. The company pays farmers 75-80% of the money it earns from milk sales, sources told PTI.Here are the revised prices of different milk varieties in Delhi-NCR:Mother Dairy sells around 35 lakh litres of milk every day in Delhi-NCR through its outlets, general trade and e-commerce platforms. Its total daily milk sales across markets exceed 50 lakh litres.The company reported a 17% rise in turnover to Rs 20,300 crore in the last fiscal year. The growth was driven by higher demand for its milk products and cooking oils.Started in 1974, Mother Dairy is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB). It sells milk and milk products under the Mother Dairy brand, edible oils under Dhara, and fresh fruits and vegetables, frozen vegetables, snacks, pulps and concentrates under Safal.Before the latest increase by Mother Dairy and Amul, Nandini had raised milk prices in Karnataka. The state Cabinet approved an Rs 8 per litre increase in the base price, with the new rates taking effect from November 1.The Karnataka government said the increase was needed to protect dairy farmers facing severe drought conditions. Law and parliamentary affairs minister Krishna Byre Gowda said the revised prices were still within the range charged in most other states.He also said rising prices of other goods had hurt farmers and milk supply in Karnataka had fallen by 10 lakh litres due to the drought this year.Cooperation minister Laxman Savadi said the government also had to consider the possibility of farmers selling their milk to other states if prices were not increased. This could have led to a shortage of milk in Karnataka.Under the revised arrangement, Rs 7 of the Rs 8 per litre increase was to go to farmers, while Re 1 was allocated to milk unions in the state.
Article Summary: Mother Dairy and Amul increase prices by Rs 2 to Rs 6 per litre. Milk fat prices have risen by around 20-25% over the past few months, while higher cattle feed prices have added to farmers' costs. Milk supplies have also tightened despite the flush season, when production and availability usually improve.

Article Title: Love over lavishness: Indriya turns Diwali into a festival of love with Aditi Rao Hydari and Siddharth
Article Text:
The festive season remains one of the most important periods for the jewellery industry, shaped by the enduring traditions of celebration, gifting and auspicious purchases.

As Indriya continues to expand its presence across India, we see this as an opportunity to build deeper emotional connections with consumers through stories that resonate with how they celebrate today. With ‘Festival of Love’, we wanted to spotlight the relationships and moments that make the festive season meaningful, while Padmika brings this sentiment to life through jewellery inspired by prosperity, blessings and new beginnings.

Together, they reflect our vision of creating jewellery that is rooted in Indian culture yet relevant for the modern consumer

A Diwali story, told in the little moments

Aaj Diwali hai ya Valentine’s Day?

This festive season, we wanted to move beyond the larger spectacle of celebration and focus on the moments of affection and connection that often unfold quietly within it.

Aditi and Siddharth brought this thought to life effortlessly. As a couple, they embody the warmth, playfulness and genuine companionship that the campaign seeks to celebrate, making the story feel authentic and relatable.

Padmika: Heritage craft through a contemporary len

Beyond the sparkle

Disclaimer: This article has been produced on behalf of Novel Jewels by Times Internet’s Spotlight team.

Every festive season, from Dhanteras and Diwali to the weddings that follow, Indians buy gold as much for tradition and sentiment as for style. And year after year, jewellery campaigns try to outdo each other with grand celebrations, sweeping visuals and big family gatherings.This year, Indriya , Aditya Birla Jewellery, has chosen a different route. Its festive campaign, Festival of Love, featuring Aditi Rao Hydari and Siddharth, sets aside the spectacle to focus on something far more familiar. The small gestures of affection that unfold between people in the middle of all the preparation.Most households will recognise the premise. Festivals bring homes alive with decorations, rituals, gifts and guests. Yet, amid the bustle, it is the simplest moments of connection that stay with us longest. For Indriya, which is steadily expanding its presence across the country, the festive season is also a chance to build a deeper bond with consumers at a time when emotion and purchase decisions go hand in hand.Sandeep Kohli, CEO, Indriya, said, “.”The campaign film follows Aditi and Siddharth as they prepare to host friends for Diwali. There is no dramatic arc. Instead, the story moves through the familiar bustle of festive preparations, punctuated by playful banter, thoughtful gestures and the easy companionship of two people entirely at home with each other. Much of the film’s charm rests on the couple’s natural chemistry, which lends it a warmth that feels lived-in rather than staged.The emotional high point arrives as the evening unfolds. A thoughtful gesture becomes the centre of attention, prompting their friends to teasingly ask, “(Is today Diwali or Valentine’s Day?)” The line lands lightly, with humour rather than sentimentality, and that is precisely its strength. In a single moment, it captures the campaign’s central idea: that love rarely announces itself, and often finds expression in the simplest, most unexpected ways.Shantiswarup Panda, Head of Marketing and Visual Merchandising, Indriya, said the intent was to look inward rather than outward. “The jewellery at the heart of the story is Padmika , Indriya’s new festive collection crafted in 22KT gold and inspired by symbols of auspiciousness. Worn by Aditi throughout the film, the collection is woven into the narrative rather than simply placed alongside it.Its defining feature is the revival of Gulabi Meenakari, a traditional pink enamel craft, enriched here with delicate blue meenakari accents. These are paired with motifs such as Goddess Lakshmi and the lotus, enduring symbols of prosperity, abundance and new beginnings. The result reinterprets familiar festive symbolism through a modern design sensibility, with necklaces, earrings, bangles and statement pieces meant to be worn through the festive season and well beyond it.In a category where festive storytelling often leans on opulence, Festival of Love makes a quiet case for restraint. By pairing a relatable narrative with a collection that honours heritage craftsmanship, Indriya positions jewellery not merely as adornment but as part of the moments and relationships that give a celebration its meaning. It is a thought worth carrying into the season: long after the diyas are put away, it is the quieter glow of love that people remember.
Article Summary: Indriya’s festive campaign, Festival of Love, features Aditi Rao Hydari and Siddharth. The jewellery at the heart of the story is Padmika, a new festive collection crafted in 22KT gold and inspired by symbols of auspiciousness.

Article Title: Taxpayer filed Form 10-IEA for old regime but chose new regime in ITR, triggering Rs 1.41 lakh demand; ITAT rejects his plea for new regime but asks taxman to allow eligible deductions under old regim
Article Text:
The tribunal examined whether the taxpayer could rely on the selection in his return when it contradicted the prescribed form he had already filed. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Akshay Nitin Malu v. Income Tax Officer

Rallis India Ltd v. Central Processing Centre

What ITAT Mumbai said

Rallis India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

You opt out of the new income tax regime by filing Form 10-IEA, but while filing your income tax return opt for the new regime. Under what regime will your return be processed - new or old?In one such case a taxpayer ended up making contrary choices and the Income Tax Department processed his return under the old tax regime and raised a tax demand. He fought the tax addition believing that his choice in ITR should override Form 10-IEA.The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Mumbai, rejected the taxpayer's argument that the selection in his return should prevail. However, it gave him partial relief. Read to know what happened.The case concerns a man’s income tax return for assessment year 2025-26. The taxpayer had opted for the new income tax regime in the preceding assessment year, 2024-25. On August 31, 2025, when he filed Form 10-IEA he opted out of the new regime and was taxed under the old income regime.However, when he filed his income tax return on September 16, 2025, declaring a total income of Rs 33,88,170, he selected the option indicating that he did not wish to opt out of the new tax regime. This was contrary to the choice that was recorded in the form he had filed earlier.The CPC processed his return under Section 143(1) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, on January 29, 2026.It took Form 10-IEA into account and raised a demand of Rs 1,41,480. Joshi sought rectification, but the CPC rejected his request under Section 154 on February 17, 2026.He then appealed to the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), who upheld the adjustment. The appellate authority reasoned that the taxpayer had opted out of the new tax regime through the prescribed form, making the contrary selection in his return an incorrect claim.Before the Mumbai ITAT, the taxpayer argued that the CPC should have followed the option selected in his return instead of relying on Form 10-IEA. His counsel cited a Pune ITAT ruling in, arguing that the choice declared in the return should be respected.He also challenged the processing of his return on the ground that the CPC had not issued prior intimation of the proposed adjustment. For this, he relied on a Bombay High Court ruling inAs an alternative, the man argued that if the old tax regime applied because of Form 10-IEA, he should be allowed the deductions available under that regime. His claims included Rs 1.5 lakh under Section 80C, Rs 50,000 under Section 80D and Rs 50,000 under Section 80TTB.The tribunal examined whether the taxpayer could rely on the selection in his return when it contradicted the prescribed form he had already filed.The bench noted that the taxpayer had opted for the new income regime in assessment year 2024-25 and subsequently filed Form 10-IEA to move to the old income tax regime for assessment year 2025-26.Under Section 115BAC, taxpayers with business or professional income must exercise the relevant option in the prescribed manner, and the rules restrict when that choice can be withdrawn.The tribunal held that the selection in the return could not override the prescribed form.It observed: “In our opinion, once a specific form has been prescribed for opting out of the new tax regime, the assessee cannot be permitted to choose for the new tax regime otherwise than filing said form under the provisions of the Act.”It also distinguished the Pune ITAT ruling cited by the taxpayer. In that case, the taxpayer had filed Form 10-IE to opt out of the new regime and had also filed the return under the old regime.This case was different because the form and the return indicated conflicting choices. The tribunal noted: “But in the instant case, facts are different. In the Form 10-IE filed, assessee is opting out of new tax regime and choosing old tax regime. But in the return of income, wrong box has been ticked.”The bench also rejected the taxpayer’s argument that the CPC had processed his return without prior intimation. It had asked him to produce evidence from the income tax portal showing that no intimation had been sent by email or physical letter, but he did not provide the requested material.The tribunal distinguished thecase because the department had acknowledged there that no notice or proposed adjustment had been issued. It therefore dismissed this ground of appeal.The taxpayer, however, succeeded on his alternative plea concerning deductions. The tribunal held that if the old income tax regime applied on the basis of Form 10-IEA, the deductions available under that regime also had to be considered.It observed: “If CPC is holding that assessee has opted out of the new tax regime and old tax regime of this is applicable, then the deduction entitled under the old tax regime should be allowed to the assessee.”The bench set aside the appellate order on this limited issue and restored the matter to the Assessing Officer to examine the eligible deductions. The tribunal also recorded that “In our opinion, there is a merit in the submission of the assessee.”The ITAT pronounced its order on September 17, 2026, and partly allowed the appeal. It did not cancel the Rs 1,41,480 demand outright or automatically grant all the deductions claimed. The Assessing Officer must examine the taxpayer's eligibility for deductions under the old regime.
Article Summary: Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Mumbai, rejected the taxpayer's argument that the selection in his return should prevail. However, it gave him partial relief. Case concerns a man’s income tax return for assessment year 2025-26. The taxpayer had opted for the new income tax regime in the preceding assessment year, 2024-25. On August 31, 2025, when he filed Form 10-IEA he opted out of the new regime and was taxed under the old income regime.

Article Title: Russia's diesel exports surge 100% after Trump lifts sanctions; not a single shipment reaches US
Article Text:
The US-bound shipments were diverted to other markets, including Brazil and Turkey

What was the Trump-Putin diesel deal?

Why deal sparked controversy?

Will Russia continue increasing diesel exports?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Russia nearly doubled its diesel exports in October after US President Donald Trump announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to increase fuel supplies to global markets. However, none of the additional shipments has reached the US so far, with tankers originally headed for American buyers changing course amid opposition to the move and concerns over sanctions.Russia exported around 271,000 barrels of diesel per day in October, compared with 135,000 barrels per day in September, according to data provider Kpler. Instead of reaching the US, the additional Russian fuel went to markets such as Brazil and Turkey, allowing Moscow to increase sales despite uncertainty over the proposed American shipments, according to a report by The Financial Times.At least two tankers initially headed for the US have changed course in recent weeks. Another vessel carrying Russian diesel, the Agioi Fanendes, remains off the US East Coast awaiting a buyer. The White House said negotiations with the vessel's owner were continuing.The increase in exports came after Washington pressed Ukraine to pause attacks on Russian oil refineries and Trump announced an agreement with Putin on October 9.Trump announced the deal last month following a conversation with Putin, saying Russia had agreed to supply additional diesel to the US and global markets to bring down fuel prices.In a social media post, Trump had said Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel, followed by another 500,000 tonnes in November and one million tonnes after that. He also said Russia would deliver another three million tonnes within a short period.The announcement came as diesel prices in the US were rising sharply, putting pressure on consumers and businesses that depend on the fuel for transport, agriculture and other operations. High fuel prices were also a political concern for Trump's Republican Party ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections.To facilitate the proposed supplies, the US Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control issued General License No. 135 on October 9. The licence temporarily authorised transactions involving the sale, delivery and import of Russian diesel that would otherwise have been restricted under US sanctions. It was issued for six months, allowing such transactions through April 2027.A White House official told the Financial Times that additional Russian diesel entering global markets would help ease prices for American consumers, even if the fuel was not delivered directly to the US.“As the President has said, this is a deal for the world. This deal was made to add diesel supply to the global market — lowering prices for Americans and the world — which is exactly what will be done,” the official said, as quoted by FT.The diesel agreement came after efforts in the US Congress to increase economic pressure on Russia over its war in Ukraine. One major measure was the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, signed into law by Trump on September 18.The legislation provided for additional sanctions against Russia and tariffs on Russian goods, as well as duties on imports from major buyers of Russian oil and gas and countries facilitating sanctions evasion. However, on October 16, Trump issued an executive order waiving the application of these measures, citing national interests and the need to pursue a peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine. It allowed up to 100% tariffs on countries buying Russian oil.A separate legal challenge has been raised by New Jersey governor Mikie Sherrill over the proposed diesel imports. In a letter dated November 2, she argued that the Treasury Department's October 9 licence conflicts with the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act, passed by Congress in April 2022. That law prohibits imports of Russian energy products, including diesel.Sherrill argued that the 2022 law does not give the president or the Treasury Department blanket authority to waive the import prohibition through a licence. She also said the administration had not met the conditions required to lift the ban and warned port and terminal operators that accepting Russian diesel could expose them to civil and criminal penalties. “New Jersey will not stand by while Donald Trump supports Vladimir Putin at the expense of Americans,” she said.The recent rise in exports may not last. Ukraine resumed attacks on Russian refineries on October 30, following a two-week pause. Russia has also extended its diesel export ban until the end of January, although some exceptions will be allowed.Richard Bronze, head of geopolitics at consultancy Energy Aspects, said the increase in exports reflected Russian refineries' ability to raise production during the pause in Ukrainian attacks. “If we want to attribute it, it would be the US pressure and Trump’s announcement of an energy ceasefire,” he said.However, Bronze expects Russian diesel exports to be “very lacklustre” in the coming months, as quoted by FT. “Russian refinery operations remain under significant pressure. We expect them to remain constrained around 4mn b/d in the near term, with limited prospects for a meaningful recovery as attacks continue,” said Sumit Ritolia, an analyst at Kpler.
Article Summary: Russia exported 271,000 barrels of diesel per day in October, up from 135,000 in September. The increase came after Washington pressed Ukraine to pause attacks on Russian oil refineries and Trump announced an agreement with Putin on October 9. None of the additional shipments has reached the US so far, with tankers originally headed for American buyers changing course amid opposition to the move and concerns over sanctions.

Article Title: India's exports jump 29.9% to $89.99 billion in October; overall trade deficit narrows
Article Text:

India's overall exports, comprising merchandise and services, rose 29.9 per cent year-on-year to $89.99 billion in October 2026, compared with $69.27 billion a year earlier, driven by a sharp increase in goods shipments, according to data released by the ministry of commerce and industry on Friday.Overall imports also increased, rising to $110.07 billion from $94.42 billion in October 2025. However, the overall trade deficit narrowed to $20.09 billion from $25.15 billion in the year-ago month, as export growth outpaced the rise in imports.Merchandise exports surged 45.06% to $49.47 billion in October from $34.11 billion a year earlier. Trade Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said India recorded its highest-ever monthly goods exports during the month, as quoted by Reuters.However, the sharp rise in goods shipments was accompanied by a widening merchandise trade gap. The goods trade deficit climbed to $39.88 billion in October, its highest level in a year, according to a Reuters calculation based on government data. This was higher than the $30.21 billion deficit recorded in September and the $32.25 billion forecast by economists in a Reuters poll.Merchandise imports rose to $89.35 billion in October from $76.69 billion in the corresponding month last year.Compared with September, exports increased from $44.40 billion, while imports rose from $74.61 billion.In the services sector, exports were estimated at $40.51 billion in October, up from $35.17 billion a year earlier. Services imports also increased to an estimated $20.72 billion from $17.73 billion.The services surplus helped offset the merchandise trade deficit, contributing to the narrowing of the overall trade gap. The ministry clarified that October services figures are estimates, as the latest actual data released by the Reserve Bank of India pertains to September.India, the world's third-largest oil consumer, imports nearly 85 per cent of its crude oil requirements. Higher import costs amid disruptions in global energy markets following the Middle East conflict have added pressure to its trade balance. A fall in Brent crude prices to around $92 a barrel has offered some relief.India's export performance has also been supported by efforts to diversify markets and expand trade ties. New Delhi has implemented trade agreements with the UK and New Zealand this year, while a trade deal with the European Union is expected to be implemented early next year.
Article Summary: India's overall exports, comprising merchandise and services, rose 29.9 per cent year-on-year to $89.99 billion in October 2026. The overall trade deficit narrowed to $20.09 billion from $25.15 billion in the year-ago month.

Article Title: OMCs continue to face petrol, diesel losses despite easing crude prices: Jefferies
Article Text:
Representative image

Crude supply improves, but freight rates remain high

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Petrochemical margins improve

Oil marketing companies (OMCs) continue to incur losses on the sale of petrol and diesel, although the extent of these losses has narrowed following a decline in crude oil prices, according to a report by brokerage firm Jefferies.Marketing losses on petrol have fallen to Rs 12 per litre, while those on diesel have eased to Rs 27 per litre, based on 15-day average pricing, the report said.In October, the corresponding losses stood at Rs 22 per litre for petrol and Rs 28 per litre for diesel.Jefferies attributed the improvement to a decline in the Indian crude basket price, which has eased to $97 per barrel from $120 per barrel in October."With the Indian crude basket price easing to $97/ bbl ($120/bbl in Oct-26), the current losses on petrol/diesel have come down to Rs12/27 per liter (Rs22/28 in Oct-26)," the report said.Despite the reduction in losses, marketing margins on both fuels remain in negative territory, indicating continued pressure on OMCs' fuel marketing operations. Jefferies noted that petrol and diesel margins had remained largely negative through much of 2026, with losses widening during periods of higher crude prices.The report also highlighted an improvement in global crude supply conditions. Crude oil exports from the Middle East have returned to pre-war levels, while Saudi Arabia's crude production rose in October to its highest level in four years.Physical premiums have also fallen to zero. However, freight rates remain very elevated, while diesel spreads continue to stay above $80, adding to pressure in the oil market.On the gas front, spot liquefied natural gas (LNG) prices averaged $31 per million British thermal units (mmbtu), down 2% week-on-week. Jefferies noted that domestic affordability remained stretched at current price levels.European Union gas storage stood at 72%, compared with 82% during the same period last year. With colder weather reducing storage levels, the brokerage expects gas prices to remain elevated as the winter season approaches.The report also pointed to an improvement in petrochemical margins over the past fortnight.A sharp decline in naphtha prices, alongside firm prices of polyethylene (PE) and polypropylene (PP), has widened spreads in the petrochemical segment.Overall, while lower crude prices have reduced the losses OMCs incur on petrol and diesel sales, their fuel marketing margins remain negative. Elevated freight rates and diesel spreads continue to weigh on the broader oil market, according to Jefferies.
Article Summary: Marketing losses on petrol have fallen to Rs 12 per litre, while those on diesel have eased to Rs 27. Jefferies attributed the improvement to a decline in the Indian crude basket price, which has eased to $97 per barrel. Elevated freight rates and diesel spreads continue to weigh on the broader oil market.

Article Title: India plans its largest strategic oil reserve in Odisha at Rs 8,571 crore cost, adding 4 million tonnes of storage as Strait of Hormuz disruptions expose supply risks
Article Text:
The proposed strategic reserve at Chandikhol has been under consideration since 2018. (Image for representative purpose only)

India’s largest strategic oil reserve

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India is stepping up efforts to enhance its strategic petroleum reserves, especially in wake of the Middle East crisis and the oil supply shock it has brought about. The government is looking for private investors to develop the country’s largest strategic petroleum reserve in Odisha.India is stepping up efforts to strengthen its strategic crude storage following the disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, which exposed the country’s vulnerability to sudden supply interruptions. The strait’s abrupt closure cut off around 40% of India’s crude supplies, leaving refiners scrambling to source alternative cargoes from across the world, often at higher costs.Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Ltd, the state-owned company responsible for operating the country’s strategic oil reserves, has issued separate tenders for developing the Odisha facility and leasing out part of the Visakhapatnam storage capacity.The project is estimated to cost Rs 8,571 crore. The proposed facility at Chandikhol will have the capacity to hold four million tonnes (MT) of crude oil, expanding the country’s existing strategic storage capacity by 80%.The government is offering financial support of up to Rs 5,142 crore for the project, according to an ET report. According to the tender documents, the contract will go to the bidder that seeks the lowest grant.Separately, the Centre plans to lease out nearly half of the storage capacity at its operational strategic petroleum reserve in Visakhapatnam. The arrangement will cover around 524,000 tonnes of capacity for three years, with an option to extend the lease by a further four years.Both moves come as oil producers in West Asia look for storage options outside the region to bypass the transit bottleneck created by the war in Iran and the prolonged disruption to energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.Last month, Saudi Arabia announced plans to start storing oil in Singapore’s rock caverns next year. The country already has crude storage facilities in Japan and South Korea. The UAE, which holds some of its crude in India’s strategic reserves, announced in June that it intended to store larger quantities in the country.The deadline for submitting bids for the new Odisha project is February 26, 2027, while bids for the Visakhapatnam storage lease must be submitted by December 1, 2026.The government has also asked Oil and Natural Gas Corp to develop 1.75 million tonnes of strategic storage capacity in Mangaluru. The state-owned oil producer approved the proposal in July.The proposed strategic reserve at Chandikhol has been under consideration since 2018, when the Cabinet cleared plans for two additional facilities: a four-million-tonne reserve in Odisha and a 2.5-million-tonne facility at Padur in Karnataka. Both projects were envisaged under the public-private partnership model to reduce the financial burden on the government.These facilities constituted the second phase of India’s strategic petroleum reserve (SPR) programme. The first phase involved building three storage facilities at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur, with a combined capacity of 5.03 million tonnes. Commissioned over the past decade, the three facilities were built at a total cost of Rs 4,098 crore.Last year, Megha Engineering & Infrastructures Ltd secured the contract to construct the 2.5-million-tonne facility at Padur as part of the second phase.The Chandikhol project, however, faced delays, partly because of the land acquisition process. According to the tender documents, the acquisition of around 400 acres at the site has now reached an advanced stage.The government also spent several years finalising a commercial structure that would attract private investors to the project. Under the model, it will provide a grant covering up to 60% of the project cost. The selected bidder will be responsible for developing and operating the commercial-cum-strategic petroleum reserve under the design, build, finance, operate and transfer model.
Article Summary: India is looking for private investors to develop the country’s largest strategic petroleum reserve in Odisha. The proposed facility at Chandikhol will have the capacity to hold four million tonnes (MT) of crude oil. The government is offering financial support of up to Rs 5,142 crore for the project.

Article Title: Tenant did not comply with 2005 Supreme Court eviction order and his son sold part of landlord’s property using parents’ settlement deed; buyer files suit against landlord but Madras HC strikes it off
Article Text:
One of the buyers alleged that the landlord’s family was interfering with her claimed peaceful possession of the property. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did the landlord’s family win while the buyer lost?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In a tenant-landlord dispute, the former is asked to vacate the property by the Supreme Court . But instead of complying, the tenant’s son ends up selling a share of the property and the buyer lodges a case against the landlord!As bizarre as it may sound, a recent Madras High Court throws light on how a tenant’s family continued to defy a Supreme Court eviction order and went on to sell the landlord’s property to two third-party purchasers.The buyers then asserted ownership rights on the strength of sale deeds executed by the tenant’s son. Read on to know what happenedThe disputed property is situated in Vathikuppam and had been rented out. The Supreme Court, through its 2005 order directed the tenant to vacate the premises by August 31, 2006 and hand over peaceful possession to the landlord.The tenant, however, did not vacate the property. He and his wife had executed a registered settlement deed in favour of their son on August 10, 2001. Their son subsequently transferred the property through two registered sale deeds. One of the sale deeds was executed in January, 2012.One of the buyers alleged that the landlord’s family was interfering with her claimed peaceful possession of the property and approached the court seeking a permanent injunction.She was aggrieved by the developments and initiated legal proceedings against the landlord and his family.She sought a permanent injunction restraining them from interfering with her claimed peaceful possession and enjoyment of the property.When the landlord questioned how the tenant’s son could sell the property, the son relied on the settlement deed executed by his parents in his favour.After the landlord and his legal heirs learnt of these transactions, they approached the District Registrar, Puducherry, seeking cancellation of the settlement deed and the sale deeds.In a 2015 order, the registrar cancelled the sale deed executed in one of the buyer’s favour.The case went on to Madras High Court, which ruled in favour of the landlord’s family by striking off the buyer’s suit seeking permanent injunction.The Madras High Court observed: “In the case in hand, it is a text book case where the tenant in the suit property, in spite of giving an undertaking before the Hon’ble Supreme Court to vacate and hand over the premises, managed to create a settlement deed in favour of his son, who, in turn, created two sale deeds.”The Madras High Court noted that the buyer had failed to disclose the earlier legal proceedings, including the Supreme Court’s eviction order, while seeking an injunction against the landlord’s family.It observed that the original tenant’s decision to execute a settlement deed in favour of his son, followed by the son transferring the property through two sale deeds to subsequent purchasers, amounted to contumacious conduct and was tantamount to contempt of court.The High Court also pointed out that the landlord and his family had been forced to run from pillar to post despite having prevailed in the earlier litigation, which had reached the Supreme Court in 2005.The court held that the buyer's suit amounted to a clear abuse of the judicial process and re-litigation.The High Court further observed that the matter warranted the exercise of its supervisory powers under Article 227 of the Constitution of India to prevent any further miscarriage of justice. It held that invoking this jurisdiction was necessary in the circumstances of the case.In 2014, the second buyer who acquired the property, moved the court through a writ petition challenging an order passed by the Tahsildar in connection with the disputed property. The Madras High Court rejected her petition on April 21, 2023, ruling that she had no rights over the landlord’s property and describing her occupation as illegal.It also ordered her eviction with police assistance.Kalpit Khandelwal, Partner at Aekom Legal, told ET that the buyer’s claim to the property hinged on the title held by the person who sold it to her, the tenant’s son. His claim, in turn, was based on a settlement deed executed by his parents, notwithstanding the Supreme Court’s direction requiring his father to vacate the premises.The Madras High Court found that the buyer had concealed details of the earlier legal proceedings.
Article Summary: Landlord was asked to vacate the property by the Supreme Court. But instead of complying, the tenant’s son sold a share of the property. The buyers then asserted ownership rights on the strength of sale deeds executed by the tenant's son. One of the buyers alleged that the landlord's family was interfering with her claimed peaceful possession.

Article Title: OpenAI lets biz to get AI requests processed in India
Article Text:
OpenAI lets biz to get AI requests processed in India

NEW DELHI: OpenAI on Thursday said eligible businesses can now have some of their AI requests processed on servers in India. The option could help banks, payments firms and other companies that need to keep certain data within the country when using AI. OpenAI already offered eligible customers the option to store data in India. The change is that the model can now process supported requests here too. If a company asks the model to summarise an internal document, for instance, the computing needed to read the document and generate the summary can take place in India.The service initially covers OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna model and is available to businesses and developers that use the company's API to build AI into their own software. To use it, customers need to set up a new project and select India as the location for both data storage and processing. The rollout is limited to direct API customers.
Article Summary: The option could help banks, payments firms and other companies that need to keep certain data within the country when using AI. The service initially covers OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna model and is available to businesses and developers that use the company's API to build AI into their own software. The rollout is limited to direct API customers.

Article Title: India at centre of global tech strategy: Costco
Article Text:
India at centre of global tech strategy: Costco

HYDERABAD: US retail giant Costco has put India at the centre of its global technology strategy as it works towards a target of $500 billion in revenue by 2033, global chief information and digital officer Javier Polit said during his first visit to the country in the role.The $300 billion retailer opened its first-ever global capability centre (GCC) in Hyderabad (became operational around Feb-March this year) after evaluating multiple international locations on talent depth, geopolitical factors and ecosystem maturity. "This is the very first GCC that Costco has in our young 50 years," Polit told TOI. He said India stood out because of its large technology workforce, more than 2,000 existing GCCs and a strong pipeline of engineering graduates. The decision, he said, was "purposeful, strategic and intentional".With Costco seeking to make its digital landscape "as agile as that of a tech company" over the next decade, Polit added that the GCC in India will also support modernisation of its legacy systems in addition to driving key tech and digital initiatives.He said Costco may also consider expanding its technology footprint beyond Hyderabad and could look at a second facility in India in the future.The company's global technology organisation has about 3,000 employees, with around 2,500 based at its headquarters in Issaquah, Washington. Dallas is its next-largest technology location, with a few hundred employees.Polit stressed that the India GCC is not being built as a low-end delivery unit. The team is already working on strategic programmes across North America, Europe and Asia, on artificial intelligence, data analytics, cybersecurity, SAP, warehouse management systems, supply chain digitisation and robotics."We don't look at this team in India as just a satellite team. They contribute and work on all the same strategic initiatives that our central team in the US does."
Article Summary: US retail giant Costco has put India at the centre of its global technology strategy. The $300 billion retailer opened its first-ever global capability centre (GCC) in Hyderabad. The decision, he said, was "purposeful, strategic and intentional"

Article Title: Chinese 'spy' Alice Huang's companies invested in DeepSeek, promised Nvidia's Blackwell chips

Alice Huang

Companies linked to alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang have invested in Chinese artificial intelligence firm DeepSeek and committed to supplying Nvidia's Blackwell chips, according to a report by The Information.Blackwell is Nvidia's latest generation of graphics processing units (GPUs) and AI accelerators. Built on the company's Blackwell GPU microarchitecture, it succeeds the older Hopper architecture and is designed to power large-scale artificial intelligence, heavy-duty data centres and high-performance computing.Alice, also known as Alice Wang or Huang Le, is a Chinese businesswoman whose links with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed have come under scrutiny.Meanwhile, Singapore authorities have issued Alice a stern warning and barred her from re-entering the country after finding that she provided inaccurate information during investigations into Megaspeed.Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said the Singapore Police Force (SPF) assessed that Alice had attempted to mislead investigators to downplay her role in the company.The probe centres on suspected false declarations involving the purchase of servers and other related offences.The SPF and Singapore Customs launched separate investigations into Megaspeed and others in February 2025.Alice's association with the Nvidia CEO reportedly dates back several years. According to reports, she was introduced to Jensen through her husband, corporate investor Kang Weigh, around a decade before reports of her alleged relationship with the billionaire executive emerged.Kang had business dealings with Jensen in the 2010s while acquiring Chinese video game companies, a source familiar with the couple told The Information.Chinese media reports suggest that Kang and Alice used their association with Jensen to secure business opportunities over the years. Some social media posts claimed that Kang would flaunt his wife's relationship with the Nvidia CEO to clients. Alice also regularly shared photographs with Jensen on her WeChat account.Her proximity to Jensen was allegedly a major factor in her business dealings in China.Their more recent business dealings reportedly took place through Megaspeed, which conducted billions of dollars in business with Nvidia. The Singapore-based data centre company remains under investigation over suspected false declarations linked to server purchases.
Article Summary: Companies linked to alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang have invested in Chinese artificial intelligence firm DeepSeek and committed to supplying Nvidia's Blackwell chips. Singapore authorities have issued Alice a stern warning and barred her from re- entering the country.

Article Title: IND vs NZ 4th ODI | 'Have you ever been dropped twice in an over?': Will Young reveals chat with Virat Kohli
Article Text:
Virat Kohli and Will Young (AFP Photo)

Young's chat with Kohli after two dropped catches

'A little bit of relief': Young on his century

Young credits partnerships for New Zealand's 333

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Is 333 enough for New Zealand?

NEW DELHI: New Zealand batter Will Young made India pay heavily for two dropped catches as he scored a brilliant 125 to help the visitors post 333 in the fourth ODI at Bay Oval on Friday. Young was dropped twice in the second over of New Zealand's innings. Rohit Sharma missed a chance at first slip off Auqib Nabi, and wicketkeeper Ishan Kishan then failed to hold on to the next delivery.Young was batting on just five at the time. He made full use of the two lifelines, scoring 125 off 88 balls to register his fifth ODI century. It was also his first hundred against India and his highest score in the format.The right-hander had managed just nine runs in the first ODI and six in the second. The third match was abandoned due to rain.After his dismissal, Young spoke about the two dropped catches and revealed a funny conversation with Virat Kohli .Young admitted that he was disappointed after the first dropped catch but was relieved to get another chance. The second miss left him laughing."Well, the first one, obviously a little bit disappointed, but at the same time relieved. The second one, you just got to laugh it off. Virat came up to me and I said, "Have you ever been dropped twice in an over?" He laughs and said no, so just brush it off and next ball."Young also explained how he changed his batting approach after getting those two lifelines."Yeah, I did actually notice that I was a little bit stuck on the crease after that, those two drops. I decided to walk at them and get my weight through the ball a bit more, and that seemed to work in my favour."Young said he was relieved to spend time at the crease and convert his start into a big score."A little bit of relief, firstly, but no, it's been amazing to spend some time in the middle. Obviously a little bit of fortune early in my innings, but I managed to stick at it and put a decent score together with a few partnerships in the middle."Young also spoke about the contributions of his fellow batters, including opening partner Tim Seifert. He said New Zealand's total was built through a series of partnerships."I try to enjoy myself the whole time. Obviously, having Seifert at the other end in the opening partnership was brilliant. He played really well, and I think it was just a story of small partnerships throughout the innings, which got us to that 333. When Finn came to the middle, he talked about enjoying it and playing with a smile on his face, so that was great to see too."Young felt New Zealand had hoped to score a few more runs but was happy with the final total after losing wickets at regular intervals."Yeah, I think at a certain stage in the innings we would have liked a little bit more, but we did keep losing wickets. So to scrap through to 333 I think is a decent score. Obviously it might be a little bit easier chasing, but I think stats say that 314 is the average first innings winning score. So hopefully that's enough. Early wickets, feel like demons, hopefully it is."
Article Summary: Will Young scored 125 to help New Zealand post 333 in fourth ODI against India. Young was dropped twice in the second over of New Zealand's innings. He made full use of the two lifelines, scoring 125 off 88 balls to register his fifth ODI century. It was also his first hundred against India and his highest score in the format.

Article Title: Thiruvananthapuram holiday on November 11: Schools and state government offices to close for Beemapally Uroos
Article Text:
Kerala holiday update: Thiruvananthapuram declares local holiday for Beemapally Uroos, public exams to continue

Holiday applicable to schools and government offices

What is the Beemapally Uroos festival?

Beemapally Dargah's significance in Kerala

Thiruvananthapuram holiday November 11: The District Collector of Thiruvananthapuram has declared a local holiday for all educational institutions and state government offices within the Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation limits on Wednesday, November 11, in connection with the annual Beemapally Uroos festival. The order applies to institutions and government offices operating within the corporation's jurisdiction.District Collector Anju K S announced the holiday as devotees prepare to participate in the annual festival at Beemapally Dargah Shareef. However, the district administration has clarified that public examinations scheduled in advance will take place according to the original timetable. The holiday declaration will not affect these examinations.The local holiday covers educational institutions and state government offices situated within the boundaries of the Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation. The closure has been announced specifically in view of the Beemapally Uroos celebrations.Students appearing for pre-scheduled public examinations should note that the examinations will proceed without changes.The district administration has confirmed that the existing examination schedule will remain in force despite the holiday.The declaration is limited to the specified municipal corporation area. The order does not state that the holiday applies across the entire Thiruvananthapuram district.The Beemapally Uroos, also known as the Chandanakudam Mahotsavam, is a prominent annual religious festival held at the historic Beemapally Dargah Shareef in Thiruvananthapuram. The 10-day celebration attracts tens of thousands of devotees, pilgrims and visitors from different parts of Kerala and beyond.The festival commemorates the death anniversaries of Saint Sayyidhathunissa Beema Beevi and her son, Ashaikhu Sayidushaheed Maheen Aboobaker, who are buried at the shrine. According to local religious beliefs, both were descendants of the family of Prophet Muhammad.Beema Beevi and her son are remembered for their healing powers, spiritual teachings and commitment to social service. Their shrine has remained an important religious destination over several generations.Beemapally Dargah Shareef is regarded as a symbol of communal harmony in Kerala. The annual Uroos festival draws visitors from different religious communities and backgrounds, making it an important gathering in the region's religious and cultural calendar.The celebrations bring together devotees and tourists, with the shrine witnessing significant visitor participation during the 10-day festival.
Article Summary: Thiruvananthapuram declares local holiday for Beemapally Uroos, public exams to continue. The holiday covers educational institutions and state government offices. Public examinations scheduled in advance will take place according to original timetable. The 10-day celebration attracts tens of thousands of devotees, pilgrims and visitors.

Article Title: Jensen Huang exits Nvidia: What it means for the AI market, investors
Article Text:
Jensen Huang.

AI market loses one of its biggest champions

Will AI companies feel the heat

What happens to the AI boom

Should Nvidia investors worry

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jensen Huang’s exit as Nvidia boss has added to uncertainty to an already nervous AI market.For months, investors have been questioning whether the AI boom is turning into a bubble. The exit of CEO Jensen Huang has raised fresh concerns about the future of the artificial intelligence bellwether.Nvidia shares plunged 13% at the opening bell, taking the company's market value below $4 trillion for the first time since July 2025. The fall dragged whole of the Wall Street in red with Dow Jones Industrial Average slipping 50.01 points, or 0.10%, to 52,436.48. The Nasdaq Composite fell 169.62 points, or 0.67%, to 25,296.57, while the S&P 500 declined 37.68 points, or 0.49%, to 7,581.70.The fall comes as investors try to understand what Huang's departure could mean for Nvidia's business, its position in the AI industry and the wider technology market.Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and turned it into one of the biggest players in the AI industry, is stepping down as CEO. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO while the company looks for a permanent successor, Nvidia said on Thursday.Huang, who owns about 3.61% of the company and is its fourth-largest investor, will also step down from the board.Huang's exit is significant because his influence went beyond Nvidia. He was one of the most prominent faces of the AI boom, and his departure has left investors wondering whether the leadership change could affect the company's growth and the wider AI industry.Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, UK, said investors were still trying to understand what the change meant for Nvidia."Investors are trying to figure out what it means exactly for the future of the company. They're putting someone as an interim just to step in. It's just a concern about what the leadership transition means for the company, whether it changes much.”The expert further told Reuters, "There's a key risk here because Jensen was seen as the kind of the front man of AI, not just at Nvidia, but in general. And him stepping down kind of adds a little bit of jitters to the market ahead of the earnings next week and obviously in the middle of this AI rout that we're going through. So it's just adds another layer of that kind of uncertainty and concern being piled onto the market."The timing is also important, with Nvidia's earnings due next week. Investors are now weighing the leadership change alongside existing concerns about the AI market.Nvidia's role in the AI industry is not limited to selling chips. Its business ties with several companies have also raised questions about how smaller players could be affected if the chipmaker changes its approach.Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey, said Nvidia's role in the industry makes its next steps important for companies that depend on it."Nvidia has been called the 'Bank of AI.' They'll sell you the chips and loan you the money. If they have to take a step back because of what's going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That's an open question."The supply of chips is another concern. If other chipmakers can meet demand, companies may still be able to continue building data centres and investing in AI. But a shortage could create problems for the industry."I have heard from some data-center folks that they can buy chips from other companies as long as those companies can supply them. If that's the case, the AI trade continues, companies keep building data centers, and life goes on. But if there's a supply shortage, then you have a problem."Huang's departure has also raised questions about whether the pace of AI development could change. Concerns over how quickly the technology is advancing and whether enough controls are in place have already been raised by Congress and others.Saluzzi told Reuters that the development could slow the industry down and give companies and policymakers time to take stock."It could also simply slow down the AI machine. Congress and others have raised concerns about the speed of AI development and whether there are proper controls and regulations. Maybe something like this slows it down, lets everyone take a breath, and acts as a kind of regulation without a regulation."Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers, Connecticut, said the news was difficult for Nvidia and the wider technology market, given how much the AI industry's expansion depends on the company's chips."It's very difficult to spin this as good news for NVIDIA. It's difficult for the tech trade right now because not only is NVIDIA's technology so central to the AI build out, but if this puts a damper on their ability to generate cash flow at the same rate they always have, that becomes tricky."Sosnick also pointed to Nvidia's many business arrangements across the industry. He said these ties had raised questions about whether they had made the AI market more stable or more fragile."The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raises the question into whether that created more stability or more fragility ... There'll be investigations. The Republicans may not investigate so much, but when you have a new Democratic Congress, I'm sure there will be all sorts of investigations as to whether export controls were violated, whether this was done with the knowledge of the, Department of Commerce and what the State Department knew about this. "For investors, much will depend on how smoothly Nvidia manages the leadership change and whether it can maintain its business momentum.Colette Kress, who is taking over as interim CEO, is well regarded by investors. However, the challenge is significant, given that Nvidia has been led by its founder since the company was set up.Gil Luria, managing director at DA Davidson, Portland, said Kress should be able to steer the company through the transition, but Huang's exit leaves a big gap in decision-making."Colette Kress is well respected by investors and should be able to guide NVIDIA through this challenging period. The task is daunting, as NVIDIA has been founder-led since inception and Mr. Huang concentrated much of the decision making," Luria said.
Article Summary: N Nvidia shares plunged 13% at the opening bell, taking the company's market value below $4 trillion for the first time since July 2025. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO while the company looks for a permanent successor. Investors are now weighing the leadership change alongside existing concerns about the AI market.

Article Title: Anthropic IPO six times oversubscribed as AI firm targets record $1.4 trillion valuation

Anthropic IPO has already been oversubscribed

Revenue growth supports valuation
