Anthropic’s upcoming initial public offering (IPO) has attracted orders for about six times the number of shares available, signalling strong investor appetite for what could become the biggest stock market listing in history.The strong demand for shares in the maker of the Claude artificial intelligence (AI) models could leave some prospective investors with smaller allocations than expected. Bankers have told investors that the company plans to prioritise existing backers, according to a Bloomberg News report citing people familiar with the matter.The reported level of demand and other details of the offering could still change.The company and some of its existing shareholders are seeking to raise as much as $64.4 billion through the IPO, while a separate private placement is expected to bring in another $26 billion. Together, the two transactions could raise around $90.4 billion, potentially making it the largest fundraising exercise of its kind.Anthropic is offering 825 million shares at a proposed price range of $70 to $78 apiece. Its shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 under the ticker symbol ANT.The company is targeting a fully diluted valuation of about $1.4 trillion.The IPO demand comes even as the AI industry faces questions over its dependence on advanced chips and the enormous spending required to develop and run AI models.Nvidia, a key strategic partner of Anthropic, has agreed to purchase about $10 billion worth of shares as part of the $26 billion private placement. Other technology companies participating in the placement include Google, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC, according to the company's filing.Anthropic has committed tens of billions of dollars towards securing access to advanced computing infrastructure, including chips needed to train and operate its AI models.Anthropic’s rapid revenue growth is a key factor underpinning its ambitious valuation. The company reported a revenue run rate of $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from the end of September, according to its filing.The figure stood at $65 billion at the end of July, Bloomberg News had earlier reported. The company calculates its revenue run rate by annualising consumption-based fees over a 28-day period and subscription fees for a single month.Anthropic has also stepped up efforts to attract investors ahead of the listing. Its chief executive officer, Dario Amodei, is scheduled to take part in a live-streamed event with JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon on Friday.Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the IPO, with 20 other banks participating in the offering.

Article Title: FBI seizes $1.2 billion in crypto stolen from Binance in record $6.3 billion heist
Article Text:
$6.3 billion were stolen form the world's largest crypto exchange last month

How did the $6.3 billion Binance heist happen?

How were the stolen funds tracked and frozen?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said Thursday that US authorities had seized or secured court authorisation to seize more than $1.2 billion worth of cryptocurrency stolen last month from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. The recovery forms part of a wider effort by US authorities and private-sector companies to track down funds taken in what is regarded as the biggest cryptocurrency heist in history.The October theft involved approximately $6.3 billion in digital assets and has been attributed by the FBI to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group. The US government and private-sector partners have so far managed to freeze more than $2.7 billion of the stolen cryptocurrency. The Justice Department said it had obtained court authorisation to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of those assets, reported AP.The latest action is part of Washington's efforts to disrupt North Korea's alleged use of cybercrime to generate funds for its government and illicit weapons programme. US authorities have repeatedly accused Pyongyang of using sophisticated cyberattacks to steal digital assets and evade international sanctions.The incident took place on October 29, when hackers drained approximately $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance wallets used to process transactions. The bulk of the theft unfolded in around 20 minutes, according to blockchain records analysed by cybersecurity firms.The precise method used to breach Binance's systems remains unclear. The exchange initially suspected that a laptop had been compromised but later said its investigation had uncovered additional points of breach.Blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs said the attackers had compromised Binance's transaction-signing infrastructure, which authorises transfers and allows funds to be moved out of wallets. In simple terms, the hackers may not have needed to steal the actual wallet keys but instead gained control over the system that authorised the release of funds.Binance had said its investigation was continuing, while its co-CEO Richard Teng assured users that losses would be covered through the company's Secure Asset Fund for Users and its own resources.After draining the wallets, the attackers attempted to move the cryptocurrency across different wallets and blockchains to avoid detection and prevent the funds from being frozen.A significant portion of the stolen assets was held in stablecoins such as Tether's USDT and Circle's USDC. Unlike decentralised cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin and Ethereum, stablecoins can be frozen remotely by their issuers, making it possible for companies to block suspicious transactions when alerted by investigators.Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis said the attackers attempted to convert hundreds of millions of dollars in stablecoins into Ethereum to move the assets beyond the reach of issuers. The firm tracked $325 million in stablecoin conversions into approximately $285 million worth of Ethereum over nearly 20 minutes.However, cryptocurrency companies, investigators and law enforcement agencies began freezing funds within hours of the attack. Chainalysis said the first freezes began at around 5:14 pm Eastern Time on October 29.The US government and private-sector partners have since frozen more than $2.7 billion worth of the stolen assets. The latest court authorisation covers more than $1.2 billion. Such cases generally involve forfeiture proceedings, in which the government files a claim before a judge determines who has a legitimate right to the recovered assets.The FBI has attributed the Binance theft to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-backed hacking group accused of targeting cryptocurrency exchanges, decentralised finance platforms and investors to generate funds for the regime.Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis said its investigators strengthened the link after observing funds stolen from Binance being mixed with cryptocurrency taken in a separate attack on exchange Bitget, which had also been attributed to North Korean hackers.North Korea has repeatedly been accused by US authorities of carrying out cryptocurrency thefts to generate revenue for its government and circumvent international sanctions. The funds are alleged to help finance the country's weapons programmes, including its prohibited nuclear and ballistic missile activities.
Article Summary: The FBI has seized or secured court authorisation to seize more than $1.2 billion worth of cryptocurrency stolen last month from Binance. The October theft involved approximately $6.3 billion in digital assets and has been attributed by the FBI to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group. US authorities have repeatedly accused Pyongyang of using sophisticated cyberattacks to steal digital assets.

The White House is weighing whether to push out commerce secretary Howard Lutnick amid mounting criticism of his handling of US export controls to China, with the controversy surrounding Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese intelligence operative adding to the pressure, according to a Reuters report.Senior White House officials have discussed whether Lutnick should be removed from his position, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday. The discussions come as lawmakers question why the Commerce Department has failed to restrict shipments of advanced US technology to Chinese companies accused of posing national security risks.The criticism predates Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO on Thursday following reports of his alleged relationships with women, including Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect of having links to Beijing's intelligence services.Lutnick's handling of the issue had already come under scrutiny following an Axios report that he spent the past year "undoing" efforts by other administration officials to hold Megaspeed, a company accused of illegally diverting US-made chips to China, accountable.According to Axios, the issue escalated during a White House Situation Room meeting after the US midterm elections, when treasury secretary Scott Bessent confronted Lutnick over the Commerce Department's failure to place Megaspeed on the Entity List.Lutnick reportedly said he would "look into it". The department denied that the confrontation took place.Reuters separately reported that the Trump administration had held off adding Chinese AI startup DeepSeek, memory chipmaker CXMT and more than 100 other companies flagged as national security risks to the trade blacklist. The US has not announced any additions to the list since October 2025, marking its longest such gap in more than a decade.Republican Senator John Kennedy said he did not know whether Lutnick should lose his job but urged him to answer questions publicly. "This is as serious as an aneurism," Kennedy said, adding that the commerce secretary would be called before Congress.Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren also demanded answers, saying: "Secretary Howard Lutnick and Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler must explain why they have not closed export control loopholes and act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China’s military."Earlier on Thursday, a White House official said President Donald Trump "maintains complete confidence in the secretary and his ability to carry out the position."Meanwhile, Trump said he had spoken to Huang on Wednesday but was unsure whether Alice Huang had been established to be a spy. The controversy has intensified following reports of additional alleged relationships involving the former Nvidia chief, including one with company vice-president Kimberly Powell.
Article Summary: The White House is weighing whether to push out commerce secretary Howard Lutnick amid mounting criticism of his handling of US export controls to China. The criticism predates Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO on Thursday following reports of his alleged relationships with women, including Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang.

Article Title: Huang high, Huang low: Nvidia's boss quits as second affair comes to light
Article Text:
Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigns as CEO following reports of alleged extramarital affairs, triggering political and corporate fallout in the US

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For 33 years, Jensen Huang held all the chips. He proved less adept at keeping his private life under wraps. On Thursday, the man who powered the AI revolution resigned as CEO of Nvidia, the company he founded and catapulted to a global #1, after a second extra-marital affair, this one with a company associate, surfaced in the media even as the first one with an alleged Chinese spy was roiling the tech and geo-political world.“Nvidia board of directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, CEO, and a member of the Board, effective immediately,” the company said in a statement, adding that Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Nvidia, has agreed to serve as Interim CEO until a permanent successor has been named. It said the Board is initiating a search for a permanent CEO and will consider internal and external candidates.“Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” the statement said. Nvidia’s ten-member board includes Indian-American Aarti Shah, formerly of Eli Lilly.Indeed, Huang, Nvidia’s only CEO since its founding in 1993, was synonymous with the company that he built into the world's most valuable semiconductor business, in the process becoming the indispensable impresario of the AI revolution.But apparently, bossing over AI and chips was easier than processing moral clarity when it came to relationships.On Wednesday evening, even as the tech and political world was still grappling with the purported Chinese honeytrap that the Nvidia honcho fell into, the New York Times reported a second extramarital affair allegedly with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice-president of healthcare, who reported directly to Huang. There was no coming back from this one.The company board initially appeared to stand by him following glowing testimonials from President Trump, who repeatedly vouched for his character despite reports of his being entrapped by a Chinese spy.The Nvidia board's November 8 statement had struck a reassuring note, expressing confidence in Huang and asserting there was no reason to believe that Nvidia's national security or corporate secrets had been compromised, while announcing an independent investigation into the matter. Four days later, the confidence evaporated after the second alleged affair, which company insiders were apparently aware of, leaked it to the NYT.Beyond the turmoil in Nvidia, where Huang’s two adult children Madison and Spencer have director-level roles, there is now considerable embarrassment for President Trump, who invested political capital vouching for Huang’s character. He called him an “honorable man” and a “great guy who… has done an amazing job for our country.” Hours after Huang quit, Trump did not address the scandal but said in a post on Truth Social, “NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!”But the fallout from the scandal goes beyond the Nvidia boardroom and the tech world. It is already shaking up Washington’s political establishment, drawing in Trump’s cabinet secretaries some of whom were at odds with each other as intelligence reports emerged over the past year of Huang’s affair with the alleged Chinese spy. Democrats are also champing at the bit to begin investigations and hearings into the matter.According to several accounts, it was secretary of state Marco Rubio, who is also the US national security advisor, who supervised a classified intelligence memorandum warning the administration about Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Rubio is also reported to have personally briefed Trump aboard Air Force One in May, before Huang joined the presidential delegation in Alaska for the onward flight to China.Trump not only allowed his favoured technology executive to travel with him to China but continued to give him character certificates, and his subsequent claim that he had not known about the intelligence concerns has now become an uncomfortable subject of scrutiny.The controversy has also drawn in two other cabinet secretaries: commerce secretary Howard Lutnick and treasury secretary Scott Bessent. According to a report in Axios, Bessent raised the question of the administration's failure to place Megaspeed, alleged to be a front company Alice Huang worked for, on the Commerce Department's Entity List, which would restrict its access to American technology. Lutnick, who like Huang has argued that excessive restrictions risk sacrificing commercial opportunities and provoking a trade war, reportedly muttered that he needed to check with Trump.Trump himself has been careful about ratcheting up temperature on the affair given an upcoming meeting next week with China’s President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, and Nvidia’s criticality to not just American tech primacy but also to the US stock market, a Trump obsession which he seems to believe is an indicator of economic health.Nvidia is not simply a chip manufacturer; its graphics processors are the picks and shovels of the AI gold rush, powering the data centers and frontier models being built by Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta and an expanding universe of AI companies. The AI boom itself has become a central engine of the US stock-market growth. Nvidia's extraordinary appreciation, the enormous capital expenditure by hyperscalers, and the enthusiasm surrounding generative AI have helped drive technology valuations and major US indices.Nvidia had gained more than 1,700 per cent over the past four years before the recent reversal.Nvidia stock fell almost 10 per cent following Huang’s resignation before recovering, even as the broader market weathered the storm -- for now.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia, the company he founded and catapulted to a global #1, after a second extra-marital affair, this one with a company associate. The New York Times reported a second extramarital affair allegedly with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice-president of healthcare, who reported directly to Huang.

Article Title: Decline in oil prices could save India up to $9bn in FY27
Article Text:
Crude oil eases after Trump's remarks

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Moderation in international crude oil prices could save India up to $9 billion on its oil import bill in the current fiscal and help temper wholesale price inflation, even as the impact on retail inflation is likely to remain limited, according to a Bank of Baroda research report.The report, authored by economist Dipanwita Mazumdar, estimates that a 10% decline in international oil prices from current levels could reduce India's oil import bill by $9-10 billion, equivalent to around 0.2% of nominal GDP. This would also support the current account deficit (CAD).International oil prices fell 22.2% between Oct 30 and Nov 10, following expectations of a possible peace agreement between the US and Iran after the US midterm elections. However, escalating attacks involving Saudi-led forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen could affect the sustainability of the decline. Brent crude futures were trading around $81 per barrel.The moderation in oil prices is expected to have a greater impact on wholesale price inflation (WPI) than consumer price inflation (CPI). Oil-sensitive components account for around 8.8% of the WPI basket. A 10% decline in crude prices could lower WPI inflation by 13-14 basis points through direct and indirect effects on petroleum products, aviation turbine fuel (ATF) and manufactured goods.The impact on CPI is expected to be largely neutral because retail prices of petrol, diesel and LPG are administered. Restaurant prices are also unlikely to respond to a temporary decline in oil prices, while the pass-through to airfares will depend on airlines and demand conditions.The report noted that consumers were largely insulated when international crude prices rose sharply, as retail fuel prices remained unchanged. A decline in global prices is therefore unlikely to translate into lower retail selling prices. However, the correction could narrow the divergence between CPI and WPI, offering some relief to manufacturers whose input costs had risen without a corresponding increase in consumer prices.On the fiscal front, higher fertiliser subsidies could increase the fiscal deficit by 0.2-0.3% of GDP. The FY27 Budget had allocated Rs 1.7 lakh crore for urea and fertiliser subsidies, including Rs 1.2 lakh crore for urea and Rs 54,000 crore under the nutrient-based subsidy (NBS) scheme.The NBS allocation has since increased to Rs 1.03 lakh crore, including Rs 41,534 crore for the kharif season and Rs 62,370 crore for the rabi season. Lower profitability of oil marketing companies could also weigh on non-tax revenue. However, higher nominal GDP growth and disinvestment receipts could provide some support to the fiscal position.Lower oil prices could also support the rupee, alongside a revival in foreign portfolio investor (FPI) inflows. Net FPI inflows rose to $7.1 billion in Nov, compared with outflows of $2.5 billion in Oct. The report attributed the revival partly to greater investor interest in emerging markets amid policy uncertainty in the US and moderation in AI-led valuations.Bank of Baroda expects the rupee to trade in the range of Rs 93-95 against the dollar in the near term, compared with its earlier forecast of Rs 94-95. However, the dollar index and expectations of tighter monetary policy in major economies remain key factors to watch.The impact of lower oil prices on bond yields is expected to be limited. While cheaper crude could provide temporary relief to India's 10-year government bond yield, global yields and domestic monetary policy are likely to keep borrowing costs elevated. The report expects another 50 basis points of rate hikes in FY27, which could limit the decline in yields.
Article Summary: Moderation in international crude oil prices could save India up to $9 billion on its oil import bill in the current fiscal. A 10% decline in crude prices could lower WPI inflation by 13-14 basis points. The impact on CPI is expected to be largely neutral because retail prices of petrol, diesel and LPG are administered.

Article Title: Turkey secures record $1.6 billion AIIB financing for climate reforms at COP31
Article Text:
AIIB strikes $1.6 billion climate deal with Turkey at COP31/Image: Reuters

Support for Turkey's emissions trading system

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Climate risks drive policy reforms

Turkey has secured a $1.6 billion financing agreement from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) to support policy reforms and attract private investment for its climate targets.The funding will help Turkey address an estimated $68 billion investment requirement for climate action by 2030, with around half of the amount expected to come from private sources, according to the AIIB. The agreement was announced on Thursday, the fourth day of the two-week UN climate conference in Antalya.The programme covers fiscal policy, financial regulation and sectoral planning. It is intended to support the implementation of Turkey's Climate Law and its emissions reduction strategy, which includes an interim target for 2035 and a commitment to reach net-zero emissions by 2053.The financing will be directed towards expanding sustainable finance, reducing emissions across industries and strengthening the country's ability to deal with climate-related risks. Turkey, which has a population of around 86 million, faces growing exposure to droughts, floods and wildfires as global temperatures rise.Konstantin Limitovskiy, AIIB's chief investment officer, said the agreement was the bank's largest climate policy-based financing package to date.The deal comes as the bank expands its climate-related lending. Its total climate financing reached a record $7.47 billion in 2025, according to the statement.A portion of the funding will help Turkey develop its emissions trading system, which is still in its early stages. Under the proposed mechanism, companies operating in high-emission industries will receive allowances that can be traded.The system could also have implications for Turkish exporters supplying goods such as steel and cement to the European Union. Under the EU's carbon border levy, carbon costs paid in Turkey can be recognised when calculating charges on emissions embedded in certain imported products. A domestic carbon pricing mechanism could therefore help exporters account for these costs.The programme has set several targets for the coming years. At least 180 industrial facilities are expected to report their baseline emissions under the trading scheme by April 2027. The plan also aims to secure production licences for 1,800 megawatts of wind and solar power capacity by early 2027.Agriculture and land management are also included in the reforms. The programme aims to help 225,000 farmers in water-stressed areas shift to crops that require less water by 2028. It also targets the designation of 50,000 hectares of land as carbon sinks by the same year, allowing these areas to absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.Turkey is facing mounting pressure from water shortages, prolonged drought, extreme heat, wildfires and flooding in urban areas. The reform programme is designed to strengthen planning and risk management across sectors affected by these threats, including water resources, ecosystems and public health.
Article Summary: The funding will help Turkey address an estimated $68 billion investment requirement for climate action by 2030. Half of the amount is expected to come from private sources. Turkey faces growing exposure to droughts, floods and wildfires as global temperatures rise. AIIB's total climate financing reached a record $7.47 billion in 2025.

Article Title: Nvidia shares crash 13% in opening trade as CEO Jensen Huang resigns; market value goes below $4 trillion

Jensen Huang scandal

Nvidia share price crash: Shares of Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, crashed in opening trade on Thursday as its CEO Jensen Huang resigned. At the stock market opening, shares of Nvidia were trading at $150.98, down 13.09%.This marks a major leadership change for the AI industry and raises questions about the future of the chipmaker Huang transformed into a dominant force in artificial intelligence. The stock crash has taken the market value of Nvidia to below $4 trillion for the first time since July 2025.The company said on Thursday that Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress would serve as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement.Nvidia also appointed former Synopysys CEO and board member Harvey Jones as the company's first chairman of the board.Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and holds a stake of around 3.61%, making him its fourth-largest investor, will also step down from the board.Nvidia shares plunged more than 12.89% in premarket trading, adding to pressure on the wider stock market.Scrutiny of Huang had intensified in recent days following reports alleging that the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of spying for Beijing.A person familiar with the matter told Reuters that Nvidia's board convened on Wednesday to discuss removing Huang. This followed reports earlier that day alleging that he had also been involved in an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported directly to him.Huang's departure leaves the $4 trillion company facing uncertainty and threatens to unsettle the wider AI ecosystem that he helped finance. Nvidia has channelled its growing cash reserves back into the industry, investing in cloud service providers, suppliers and some of the world's largest AI research labs.Investor confidence in AI-related stocks has already weakened amid concerns about mounting cash burn and increasing debt among technology companies that have traditionally generated substantial cash. These developments have raised questions about whether the massive investments underpinning the AI boom will ultimately deliver the expected returns.Huang's exit could also have significant implications for US policy on chip exports, given his efforts to maintain access to the Chinese market and his close relationship with US President Donald Trump.On Sunday, Trump said Huang had "done an amazing job for our country". He also said the Nvidia chief had told him he was unaware that the Chinese woman with whom he had an affair was a spy.A departure by Huang could "leave a vacuum at the top", said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth a few hours before the announcement of Huang’s resignation."They're going to have to find a successor that will help the market feel comfortable in the leadership and the direction the company will take."Beyond the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia, investors are increasingly concerned that the broader AI industry could lose momentum. Questions have persisted over whether the technology will generate sufficient profits to justify the enormous sums being invested in its development.Analysts also noted that some investors could be willing to take a gamble by buying Nvidia shares at what appears to be a discounted price, despite uncertainty over the implications of Huang's troubles for the company.“There is no credible way to put a precise revenue loss on his departure,” Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote told AP.“Customers buy Nvidia’s computing power, software and networking ecosystem, and those advantages wouldn’t disappear with its CEO,” she said.
Article Summary: Shares of Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, crashed in opening trade on Thursday as its CEO Jensen Huang resigned. At the stock market opening, shares of Nvidia were trading at $150.98, down 13.09%. This marks a major leadership change for the AI industry and raises questions about the future of the chipmaker.

Article Title: Wall Street today: Nvidia tumbles 12% in pre-market trading as Jensen Huang steps down as CEO
Article Text:
Nvidia in free fall: Share price tumles over 12%

Other AI stocks fall too

Dollar, bond yields add to market pressure

Nvidia in focus

US stock futures slid on Thursday as Nvidia shares plunged over 12% after Jensen Huang stepped down as the chipmaker’s CEO, triggering a broader sell-off in artificial intelligence-linked stocks. The leadership shake-up at the $4 trillion company rattled investor sentiment, adding to concerns over an AI sector already grappling with funding uncertainties and regulatory scrutiny.Dow futures edged down 23 points, or 0.04%, to 52,555, while S&P 500 futures shed 43.75 points, or 0.57%, to 7,596.75. Nasdaq futures led the losses, falling 352.25 points, or 1.24%, to 28,121, as Nvidia shares plunged 12.50%.Nvidia's board had met on Wednesday to discuss Huang's position after allegations that the 63-year-old had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of spying for Beijing. Reports also alleged that he had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive who reported to him.The controversy has raised concerns about the future of the $4 trillion chipmaker and the wider AI ecosystem, which Huang helped build by directing Nvidia's growing cash reserves towards cloud providers, suppliers and major research laboratories. The company's practice of financing infrastructure built around its chips has also attracted scrutiny over circular funding.The sell-off spread across AI-linked companies, with Oracle shares falling 3%, Micron Technology dropping nearly 5% and Intel declining more than 3%. Neocloud company Nebius fell 13% in premarket trading despite reporting better-than-expected third-quarter revenue, as its guidance disappointed investors. Advanced Micro Devices, however, moved higher after receiving an upgrade from William Blair.In Hong Kong, Alibaba and Tencent fell 6.7% and 2.6%, respectively, amid concerns that Washington could restrict access to offshore data centres equipped with advanced processors. The dollar touched a 19-month high, while the US 10-year Treasury yield climbed back to 5% amid growing expectations of another Federal Reserve rate hike next month.The dollar has gained more than 1.5% since stronger-than-expected US inflation data prompted investors to reassess interest rate expectations. US President Donald Trump added to uncertainty after saying in a Truth Social post, "We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed."As Jensen Huang steps down, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO following Jensen Huang's departure, the chipmaker said on Thursday. She will lead the company while it searches for a permanent successor.Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013 as executive vice-president and chief financial officer and has held the position since. During her tenure, the company's revenue grew from $4.13 billion in the fiscal year she joined to $215.9 billion in fiscal 2026, reflecting Nvidia's massive business expansion.She has also regularly joined Huang on the company's quarterly earnings calls, where Nvidia discusses its financial performance and outlook. Her appointment brings a long-serving finance executive to the helm of the chipmaker, whose processors are widely used in advanced computing systems and artificial intelligence data centres.Investors are now looking towards Nvidia's earnings next Tuesday for further cues on the AI trade. Saxo Bank's Chief Investment Strategist Charu Chanana said, "Strong results could reaffirm the AI growth story, but may not fully remove the governance discount."Jake Dollarhide, chief executive officer at Longbow Asset Management, said the controversy could weigh on the company."I believe the board won't oust him until they have an all-star, a known entity in the tech sector, to replace him," he said. "At the end of the day, let's not forget that the Nvidia chip is the centrepiece of the AI story."
Article Summary: US stock futures slid on Thursday as Nvidia shares plunged over 12% after Jensen Huang stepped down as the chipmaker’s CEO. The leadership shake-up at the $4 trillion company rattled investor sentiment, adding to concerns over an AI sector grappling with funding uncertainties and regulatory scrutiny.

Article Title: 1.14 lakh startups generate more than 12 lakh jobs in India: Finance ministry

Finance Ministry

NEW DELHI: More than 1.14 lakh startups in India have created over 12 lakh jobs so far, the finance ministry said in its latest review of the Indian economy.In the report titled, ‘The Indian Economy: A Review January 2024’, the Department of Economic Affairs said that the 1.14 lakh startups recognised by the government under the 'Startup India initiative’ created more than 12 lakh jobs (as of October 2023).The state-owned e-commerce platform Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) clocked more than 63 lakh transactions till November 2023, the document read.Despite facing global challenges in 2023 like valuation issues, few IPOs, regulatory changes and macroeconomic and geopolitical trends, India remains the third largest tech start-up ecosystem globally, with over 950 tech startups founded last year.The cumulative funding for more than 31,000 tech start ups has exceeded $70 billion (from 2019 to 2023), according to a recent report by Nasscom in collaboration with Zinnov.“In 2023, despite facing global economic and regulatory challenges, Indian tech startups have prioritised the imperative of enhancing their business fundamentals, driving profitability and growth,” said Debjani Ghosh, President, Nasscom.“The proliferation of tech startups in tier 2 and 3 cities marks the ecosystem's resilience,” she added.Navigating 2024, tech startup founders expect to continue the revenue growth path with measured steps focusing on optimising expenditure and maximising profitability for B2B tech startups.Investments in deeptech will continue an upward trend in 2024. With generative AI (GenAI) acceleration, 70 per cent of start-up founders are embedding artificial intelligence (AI) in their solutions.As funding becomes scarce for the Indian startup ecosystem in general, the explosion of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has given a new lease of life to entrepreneurs and founders in the country, as the Centre extends support to the sector.
Article Summary: The state-owned e-commerce platform Open Network for Digital Commerce clocked more than 63 lakh transactions till November 2023. India remains the third largest tech start-up ecosystem globally, with over 950 tech startups founded last year. The cumulative funding for more than 31,000 tech start ups has exceeded $70 billion.

Article Title: Startups Revolutionizing Carbon Dioxide into Valuable Products
Article Text: For most perfume makers, ingredients to make it smell great are the most important feature. But for Stafford Sheehan, a cofounder and chemist at Air Company, the most important part of perfume-making has no scent at all.New York-based Air Company uses technology that converts planet-warming carbon dioxide into ethanol, which is then blended with essential oils and water to produce perfume. While the pale yellow-color Air Eau de Parfum is about 50% more expensive than Coco Chanel’s signature No. 5, Sheehan says his product is uniquely valuable: Every 50-milliliter bottle uses 3.6 grams of CO2 that otherwise would have been released into the atmosphere. Its package reads: “Turning CO2 into something beautiful.”While the volume of CO2 utilized in the bottle is extremely small, Air Company’s perfume showcases one way the coming wave of captured carbon can be put to use. Renewable energy and electric cars alone won’t be enough to cut CO2 emissions to zero. The world will almost certainly need to capture billions of tons of the gas annually in the coming decades. Large amounts will likely be stored underground.Using it — so-called carbon capture and utilization, or CCU — to create new products from perfume to jet fuel could be an important tool in the fight against climate change, too, though the nascent industry has major hurdles to overcome.Roughly 230 million tons of CO2 are utilized every year, according to a 2019 report by the International Energy Agency. While roughly one-third of that is reused to force more oil from the ground — hardly a carbon-neutral process — CCU advocates say that the number of companies coming up with new uses for carbon has mushroomed in recent years, paving a way to unlock climate benefits. Carbon-derived fuels and chemicals, for example, could theoretically grow to the scale of billions of tons of CO2 use per year if companies could perfect their technology and lower costs.Calgary-based CleanO2 transforms CO2 captured from building heating boilers into feedstock to make soap. Newlight Technologies, a biotechnology startup based in California, takes carbon pulled directly from the air and turns it into biodegradable plastics. Germany’s Covestro AG, one of the world’s largest polymer manufacturers, is also switching some of its fossil fuel-based feedstocks to carbon-derived materials for everything ranging from car shells to medical devices and stadium roofs.Most companies working on CO2-sequestering products are still in their infancy. To grow the emerging sector, global venture capitalists in 2022 poured nearly $500 million into carbon utilization businesses, according to the IEA. That’s in stark contrast to 2015, when barely any venture money went to technologies that utilize CO2.“It’s just a whole different landscape today than it was a decade ago,” says Sasha Mackler, executive director of the energy program at Washington, DC-based non-profit Bipartisan Policy Center.Jennifer Holmgren, chief executive officer of LanzaTech Global Inc., has experienced the shifting sentiment firsthand. The Illinois-based company uses a carbon-eating bacteria – discovered in the guts of rabbits and preserved as powder – to make alternative ethanol in bioreactors not dissimilar to how breweries ferment beer. In the early 2010s, when Holmgren touted carbon-derived ethanol to prospective customers, her sales pitch was met with skepticism.But the tide began turning later that decade. In 2018, the company’s jet fuel produced from the emissions of a Chinese steel mill helped power a Transatlantic flight. LanzaTech has also inked agreements with airlines including Japan’s All Nippon Airways to supply CO2-derived jet fuel. And LanzaJet, the company’s spin-off, plans to start producing sustainable jet fuels at a commercial scale this year.Yet for all the hype around sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) using captured carbon, the industry is still an extremely small player. Almost every major airline in the world has pledged to use at least 10% sustainable jet fuels by 2030, yet SAF makes up only 0.1% of global aviation fuel supply — and much of it is made from sources other than captured CO2, such as used cooking oil.“There’s a lot more interest because consumers have become much more interested in buying things that are lower carbon,” says Holmgren. That’s enabled LanzaTech to expand the number of products that utilize CO2.American plastic container maker Plastipak, for instance, has partnered with LanzaTech to produce carbon-derived packaging materials, while polyester converted from LanzaTech’s ethanol has replaced its petroleum-based counterpart at a pilot scale in Lululemon shorts, Zara dresses, H&M yoga pants, On running shoes and Craghoppers jackets. Like SAF, though, there’s still a long way to go for CO2-derived polyester to reach meaningful levels of use.Momentum to grow beyond one-off products and low-scale production has also been supercharged by a growing array of regulations and incentives around the world. For instance, the Inflation Reduction Act that US President Joe Biden signed in 2022 raised the tax credit for carbon capture and utilization by more than 70% to $60 per metric ton in an effort to make costly projects more financially appealing.To keep the climate within habitable limits, the IEA estimates that carbon capture will have to grow to 7.6 billion tons of CO2 annually by mid-century. CCU will play a role, though just how big remains to be seen. Not every use case is created equal and some approaches, such as dissolving compressed CO2 in water to make carbonated beverages, only store the gas temporarily. To quantify the true climate benefit of carbon utilization, experts say third-party verification is badly needed.The rise of CCU technology comes as another key approach in President Biden’s net-zero roadmap is hitting a bit of a wall. Carbon capture and storage — that is, gathering CO2 as it’s released from a coal-fired power plant or other emissions source and sequestering it underground — has faced challenges because carbon is often captured in one place and stored in another. That requires pipelines to transport the gas, which many local communities have opposed. Blackrock-backed Navigator, for example, recently announced it was scrapping a planned 1,300-mile CO2 pipeline.Carbon utilization companies say that they can sidestep that issue by using carbon near or at where it’s captured.At its 12-acre factory in Brooklyn, Glenwood Mason Supply demonstrates how. The concrete manufacturer takes CO2 captured at a residential building by its partner company, CarbonQuest, and uses a technique licensed from low-carbon concrete startup CarbonCure to convert the compressed carbon into a powder not unlike dry ice. It then injects it into industrial mixers. There, the CO2 meets cement, sand and aggregate, setting off a series of chemical reactions. The final result is concrete blocks with CO2 sealed in.The technique not only stores carbon but it can also make the blocks marginally stronger. The company estimates that it has utilized about 100 tons of CO2 in total since 2020. Even if the blocks break down, the stored carbon won’t be released as CO2 because it’s been mineralized.“Cement is a big offender in carbon emissions,” says Constance Cincotta, founder of the concrete factory. She became intrigued by the technology and its ability to lower her company's climate impact after hearing about it at an industry conference in the early 2010s. But it wasn't until CarbonCure came on the scene a few years ago that the prospect of CO2-storing cement became tangible. Glenwood Mason then sourced CO2 locally from CarbonQuest, which captures carbon from buildings in New York. Those factors have enabled large-scale production.While Cincotta’s intended to help the planet, she and her team discovered that sinking CO2 into concrete blocks is good for the business, too. In 2019, New York City — where the majority of the company’s concrete blocks are sold — passed a regulation requiring all buildings to shrink their carbon footprint 40% by the end of the decade. Glenwood Mason’s phones have been ringing ever since, with calls from architects and property developers who want to leverage their lower-carbon building materials to cut emissions, says Jeff Hansen, the company’s vice president in architectural sales and marketing.The factory’s CO2-storing concrete blocks also caught the eye of Amazon.com Inc, which in 2022 persuaded a real estate developer to purchase roughly 50,000 blocks for the construction of a new warehouse in New York that Amazon has leased. Had Glenwood Mason not sealed CO2 in its blocks, it wouldn’t have won the contract, Hansen says. To figure out how to pack more carbon into its products, the company has set up a laboratory in its factory to test the reaction between CO2 and other concrete feedstocks under different temperatures and humidity levels.But figuring out the right formula is only one consideration. Utilizing CO2 often comes with an additional cost. As the demand for CO2-derived products climbs, that green premium is expected to go down. Yet “it’s very hard to be a cost parity with a 100-year-old industry that doesn’t even have to pay for its externalities,” says Holmgren of LanzaTech. Even with economies of scale, Holmgren estimates that carbon-containing fabrics will still likely cost as much as 20% higher than conventional ones.“It’s unlikely that we will ever be a cost parity,” she says.In addition to the cost barrier, CCU companies also have to convince end users that may be suspicious of unproven new technologies.Changing feedstocks “does come with risks,” says Keith Wiggins, chief executive officer of Econic Technologies, a British startup that specializes in making carbon-derived chemicals. To get risk-averse industries onboard, Wiggins says his company is laser-focused on those that are under consumer pressure to change course.That strategy seems to be working. Econic has teamed up with three manufacturers in the US, China and India to produce mattresses, outdoor garments and building insulation materials that utilize CO2. The first batch of products using the company’s technology are scheduled to enter the market in 2024.For all the promise of the carbon utilization industry, it remains to be seen if it can challenge the status quo. While Air Company started selling carbon-derived perfume in 2021, the startup has yet to build its first commercial plant, Sheehan says, citing the time-consuming process needed for collecting data and fine-tuning the technology for large-scale production.Fow now, the company’s demonstration facility in New York City — where CO2 and hydrogen gas flow through tubes into a reactor to form chemical reactions, aided by catalysts made from a confidential mixture of metals — is designed to yield at least 10,000 gallons of CO2-derived liquid annually. The limited production capacity has left many orders for its perfume — as well as jet fuels and Air Vodka, another popular product made from CO2 — unfilled.“We need to scale these facilities to the size of oil refineries today in order to have the impact on climate change that we want to have,” Sheehan says.
Article Summary: New York-based Air Company uses technology that converts planet-warming carbon dioxide into ethanol, which is then blended with essential oils and water to produce perfume. Carbon-derived fuels and chemicals, for example, could theoretically grow to the scale of billions of tons of CO2 use per year if companies could perfect their technology.

Article Title: E-commerce firm Udaan raises $340 million ahead of planned IPO
Article Text: Indian e-commerce firm Udaan raised $340 million to strengthen its supply chain and boost vendor partnerships ahead of a stock market debut planned for 2025.The Series E round was done via a combination of fresh equity and conversion of debt, the Bangalore-based company said in a statement Thursday. The round was led by M&G Plc and existing investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners and DST Global participated.The round “fully funds our business plan,” Vaibhav Gupta, Udaan co-founder and chief executive officer, said in the statement. “It enables our continued journey of growth and profitability, positioning us well to be public-market ready in the next 12-18 months.”Udaan, which competes with Reliance Industries Ltd. and Walmart Inc.’s Flipkart in helping smaller merchants source their goods, runs an online marketplace and logistics networks that help mum-and-pop stores get quicker deliveries and cut traditional middlemen out. That kind of digital-led wholesale business, though a very small part of India’s overall retail market, is expected to swell to $150 billion in sales in a decade, according to McKinsey & Co.The startup targets an initial public offering in 2025, though it’s yet to decide whether it will do so in India or overseas, Gupta told Bloomberg News last month.Udaan was founded in 2016 by three engineers who previously worked at Flipkart. The trio together ran the company until Gupta, one of the founders, took over as CEO in 2021. The other two founders — Amod Malviya and Sujeet Kumar — are board members.
Article Summary: Indian e-commerce firm Udaan raised $340 million to strengthen its supply chain. The Series E round was done via a combination of fresh equity and conversion of debt. The startup targets an initial public offering in 2025, though it’s yet to decide whether it will do so in India or overseas.

Article Title: Minuscule AI startup raises $41 million to tap India growth
Article Text: A generative artificial intelligence startup targeting the Indian market raised $41 million in fresh funding, the largest such round by an early-stage AI contender in the country.Sarvam AI is building large language models targeted at unique uses in Indian languages at price points that the country’s 1.4 billion people can afford. The Series A funding round was led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, and participants included Silicon Valley billionaire Vinod Khosla’s Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners, formerly Sequoia Capital India & Southeast Asia, Sarvam said Thursday.The Bangalore-based startup, until recently in stealth mode, was co-founded by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar. It has ambitious plans to build open source foundational AI systems as well as tools for creating apps for the meager compute infrastructure available to developers in India. The startup has a total of 18 employees and is just opening an office in the city."What we are showing is that you can build large language models with limited resources,” Raghavan said in a phone interview. "We are building at a smaller scale and demonstrating that these can be extremely cost and energy efficient so they can be accessed by everyone."Large language models, like OpenAI’s GPT-4 and Meta Platforms Inc.’s Llama, are powerful AI systems that understand by learning from vast amounts of diverse data from the internet and elsewhere to summarize, translate, and create text, audio and video for a wide range of applications. The rivalry to develop ever-more sophisticated models is heating up in Silicon Valley and such efforts have attracted billions of dollars in investments.
Article Summary: Sarvam AI is building large language models targeted at unique uses in Indian languages. The Bangalore-based startup, until recently in stealth mode, was co- founded by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar. It has ambitious plans to build open source foundational AI systems.

Article Title: ZestMoney set to shut operations this month
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Buy now Pay Later (BNPL) startup ZestMoney has decided to shut operations. The move will impact some 150 employees of the firm, the company's management told employees in a town hall on Tuesday. ZestMoney did not comment. It is learnt that the firm will shut down by the end of this month.The move comes after attempts by the Bengaluru-based startup to get acquired by larger peer PhonePe failed. The deal was called off earlier this year after a due diligence process undertaken by PhonePe, while evaluating the potential acquisition failed to meet its bar. The Walmart-owned fintech major had, however, hired some 130 of ZestMoney's employees.

The move comes after attempts by the Bengaluru-based startup to get acquired by larger peer PhonePe failed. The Walmart-owned fintech major had, however, hired some 130 of ZestMoney's employees.
